problem_text:
A city planner needs to distribute a fixed budget across 18 community development projects to maximize overall social benefit.  
The profile of each project is given below:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.128, impact factor 0.250, allocation range [0.076, 0.475]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.046, impact factor 0.071, allocation range [0.039, 0.387]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.140, impact factor 0.222, allocation range [0.053, 0.431]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.164, impact factor 0.245, allocation range [0.028, 0.749]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.147, impact factor 0.213, allocation range [0.070, 0.741]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.128, impact factor 0.025, allocation range [0.020, 0.305]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.076, impact factor 0.261, allocation range [0.086, 0.736]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.198, impact factor 0.062, allocation range [0.039, 0.645]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.042, impact factor 0.151, allocation range [0.013, 0.707]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.199, impact factor 0.124, allocation range [0.075, 0.893]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.147, impact factor 0.295, allocation range [0.058, 0.389]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.106, impact factor 0.201, allocation range [0.081, 0.870]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.169, impact factor 0.256, allocation range [0.085, 0.556]  
* Project N: benefit score 0.109, impact factor 0.297, allocation range [0.071, 0.805]  
* Project O: benefit score 0.147, impact factor 0.169, allocation range [0.046, 0.856]  
* Project P: benefit score 0.088, impact factor 0.108, allocation range [0.016, 0.358]  
* Project Q: benefit score 0.197, impact factor 0.207, allocation range [0.014, 0.884]  
* Project R: benefit score 0.080, impact factor 0.297, allocation range [0.070, 0.408]  

Each project must receive a share of the total budget within its specified range, and all shares must sum to 1.  
To ensure timely completion, the subset of high-priority projects L = {A, B, D, E, H, I, L, M, N, O, P, Q, R} must together receive at least 0.647 of the total budget.  
Additionally, the total community disruption, measured by a composite impact index, must not exceed 0.242, and the overall benefit score must be at least 0.104.  
Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
